Philosophy (BA)

Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

Overview

The Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy develops rigorous analytical reasoning, clear writing and the ability to evaluate arguments across ethics, metaphysics, epistemology and the history of philosophy. Majors work closely with faculty in small seminars and complete a capstone in their senior year.

Students considering graduate study in philosophy are encouraged to complete the honors thesis. The department also cooperates with the School of Law on a pre-law advising track for interested undergraduates.

Admission Requirements

Admission follows the university's undergraduate admission requirements described in the Admission and Orientation section of this catalogue. No supplemental application is required for the major.

Degree Requirements

The degree requires a minimum of 128 units, including general education, and at least 32 upper-division units in philosophy. A grade of C (2.0) or better is required in each course counted toward the major. A cumulative GPA of at least 2.0 in all USC course work is required for graduation.

Lower-Division Requirements

  • PHIL 100 The Big Questions (4 units)
  • PHIL 222 Introduction to Logic (4 units)

Upper-Division Requirements

Choose eight courses (32 units) from the following, including at least one course in the history of philosophy and one course in value theory:

  1. PHIL 340 Ancient Philosophy (4 units)
  2. PHIL 341 Modern Philosophy (4 units)
    • Recommended preparation: PHIL 100
    • Satisfies the history of philosophy distribution
  3. PHIL 430 Ethics (4 units) 1
  4. PHIL 450 Epistemology (4 units)

Residency and Transfer

At least 20 of the 32 upper-division units must be completed in residence at USC. No more than two courses taken on a Pass/No Pass basis may count toward the major. Double-counting toward another major is limited to two courses with advisor approval.

1 PHIL 430 requires junior standing. Students may substitute PHIL 431 Advanced Ethics with written approval of the undergraduate advisor.

For departmental scholarship opportunities see the Dornsife scholarship page.
